Hi, could you please write a reply to my landlord about the late fee? I paid on time.

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

baseline_runs.answer:
Here's a reply you can send by email, which the lease allows under Section 9.4:

---

Subject: Re: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi Dana,

Thank you for your message. I'm writing to dispute the $75 late fee added to my account for this month.

Rent was received on the 3rd, which falls within the grace period described in Section 4.2 of my lease. That section states that rent is due on the 1st, a grace period applies through the 5th, and no late fees may be charged during the grace period. Because my payment was made within that window, I don't believe the fee is valid.

Could you please remove the $75 charge from my account and send me written confirmation once it's done? Please let me know if you need any documentation from my end, such as a copy of the payment confirmation or receipt.

I'm glad to keep paying on time and want to keep this resolved smoothly. Thank you for looking into it.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B, Maple Court Apartments
[Date]

---

Before sending, attach or reference your payment confirmation showing the date it was received. If the fee isn't removed, you can follow up in writing and, if needed, contact your local tenant rights office or housing authority.
